key_insight: Evolution Strategy can directly learn a recurrent wall controller on a large turbulent channel and achieve stronger drag reduction than prior gradient-based policies, reaching about 26% skin-friction reduction.
engineering_relevance: This suggests black-box evolutionary optimisation may be a practical route to robust closed-loop flow control when gradient-based controllers overfit small domains or fall into degenerate actuation patterns.
method: Recurrent closed-loop controller optimised with Evolution Strategy on a full turbulent channel at Reτ≈180.
Policies evaluated over complete flow episodes with an energy-aware objective and parallel candidate processing.
Performance compared against GRU-MARL and classical opposition control.
evidence_signal: The ES controller reduced skin-friction drag by about 26%, outperforming GRU-MARL trained on a minimal box (17%) and slightly exceeding opposition control (22%), with supporting friction, Reynolds-stress, and anisotropy analyses.
watch_item: Training and evaluation are done at Reτ≈180, so robustness, cost, and transferability to higher-Re flows and hardware must still be verified.
paper_title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction
